subject: Physics
question: A point on the rim of a wheel of radius 0.40 m completes one revolution every 0.50 s. Calculate the angular velocity of the wheel and the speed of the point in km h⁻¹.
response_text:
Given: r = 0.40 m, T = 0.50 s.

Angular velocity: ω = 2π/T = 2π/0.50 = 4π ≈ 12.6 rad s⁻¹
Linear speed: v = ωr = 12.6 × 0.40 = 5.03 m s⁻¹ ≈ 5.0 m s⁻¹
In km h⁻¹: 5.03 m s⁻¹ × 3.6 = 18.1 km h⁻¹

Every point on the rim moves at about 18 km h⁻¹, but the angular velocity is the same for every point on the wheel.

correct_steps: Every point on the rim moves at about 18 km h⁻¹
